entities.summary: Páramo may refer to a variety of alpine tundra ecosystems located in the Andes Mountains in South America. Some ecologists describe the páramo broadly as "all high, tropical, montane vegetation above the continuous timberline". A narrower term classifies the páramo according to its regional placement in the northern Andes of South America and adjacent southern Central America. The páramo is the ecosystem of the regions above the continuous forest line, yet below the permanent snowline. It is a "Neotropical high mountain biome with a vegetation composed mainly of giant rosette plants, shrubs and grasses".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The páramo ecosystem plays a crucial role in maintaining biodiversity and regulating local climate patterns in the Andes Mountains. Its unique vegetation composition provides habitat for endemic species and helps mitigate the effects of climate change.
